He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball|Delaware Blue Hens]] and the [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's Hawks]]. ==Early life== Ryan Daly helped the St. Denis Bulldawgs win the Region 32 Championship in 2010. Daly played for [[Archbishop John Carroll High School]] in [[Radnor, Pennsylvania]], where he was teammates with future NBA player [[Derrick Jones Jr.|Derrick Jones Jr]].{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Matt |title=Carroll's supporting cast can't pull it through in AAA title game |url=https://www.delcotimes.com/news/boys-basketball-carroll-s-supporting-cast-can-t-pull-it-through-in-aaa-title-game/article_afdf5fb1-bb66-59ed-8fb4-6378f90a21f4.html |website=[[Delaware County Daily Times]] |accessdate=July 21, 2020 |date=March 21, 2015}} In his junior season, he averaged 12.8 points per game, helping his team reach the Class AAA state title game.{{cite web |last1=Verlin |first1=Josh |title=Hartford gets commitment from Carroll guard Ryan Daly |url=https://www.cityofbasketballlove.com/news_article/show/541640-hartford-gets-commitment-from-carroll-guard-ryan-daly |publisher=City of Basketball Love |accessdate=July 21, 2020 |date=August 7, 2015}} As a senior, Daly averaged 21.7 points and seven rebounds per game, making 65 three-pointers and leading his team to second place in the [[Philadelphia Catholic League]].{{cite web |last1=De George |first1=Matthew |title=Boys Basketball All-Delco: Albeit at Carroll, Daly follows in father's footsteps |url=https://papreplive.com/2016/03/31/boys-basketball-all-delco-albeit-at-carroll-daly-follows-in-fathers-footsteps/ |publisher=PA Prep Live |accessdate=July 21, 2020 |date=March 31, 2016}} Daly was named Catholic League [[most valuable player|Most Valuable Player]], Markward Club City Player of the Year, while earning Class AAA All-State First Team honors.{{cite web |last1=Selagy |first1=Christy |title=Game Day Feature: Ryan Daly |url=https://sjuhawks.com/news/2018/12/29/211781190.aspx |publisher=Saint Joseph's University |accessdate=July 21, 2020 |date=December 29, 2018}} He had originally committed to play college basketball for [[Hartford Hawks men's basketball|Hartford]] but never officially signed with the program. Daly switched his commitment to [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball|Delaware]] after Archbishop Carroll alum [[Martin Ingelsby]] was hired as its head coach.{{cite web |last1=Tresolini |first1=Kevin |title=Landing with Blue Hens a dream come true for Daly |url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/college/ud/2016/05/26/landing-blue-hens-dream-come-true-daly/84979572/ |website=[[The News Journal]] |accessdate=July 21, 2020 |date=May 26, 2016}} ==College career== ===Delaware=== On January 7, 2017, Daly scored a freshman season-high 28 points for Delaware in a 91–81 loss to [[UNC Wilmington Seahawks men's basketball|UNC Wilmington]].{{cite web |title=Bryce hits for 27pts as UNC Wilmington tops Delaware, 91-81 |website=[[KSL-TV]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.ksl.com/article/42807086/bryce-hits-for-27pts-as-unc-wilmington-tops-delaware-91-81 |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=January 7, 2017}} He made a game-winning three-pointer with 12 seconds left, while recording 24 points and 12 rebounds, in a 68–67 victory over [[Drexel Dragons men's basketball|Drexel]] on February 16, 2017.{{cite web |title=Ryan Daly hits game-winning 3 to lift Delaware over Drexel |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/ncaa/ryan-daly-hits-game-winning-3-lift-delaware-basketball-over-drexel-basketball |website=[[NBC Sports]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=February 16, 2017}} He registered six [[double-double]]s and set school freshman records for points and rebounds.{{cite web |title=Ryan Daly - Men's Basketball |url=https://bluehens.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ryan-daly/8706 |publisher=University of Delaware Athletics |accessdate=August 9, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Tresolini |first1=Kevin |title=Daly news: Blue Hen guard named CAA rookie of the year |url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/college/ud/2017/03/02/daly-news-blue-hen-guard-named-caa-rookie-year/98596302/ |website=[[The News Journal]] |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=March 2, 2017}} Daly was named [[Colonial Athletic Association]] (CAA) Rookie of the Year, winning CAA Rookie of the Week six times, and earned Third Team All-CAA honors.{{cite web |title=The Future of Delaware Basketball: Freshman Phenom Ryan Daly |url=https://herosports.com/ncaa-basketball/ryan-daly-delaware-basketball-future-college-basketball-bqbq/ |publisher=HERO Sports News |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=March 2, 2017}} As a freshman, he averaged 16 points, 7.4 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=McCue |first1=Owen |title=Ryan Daly to finish college career at Saint Joseph's |url=https://www.cityofbasketballlove.com/news_article/show/905633 |publisher=City of Basketball Love |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=April 8, 2018}} In his sophomore season, Daly averaged 17.5 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game and was named to the Third Team All-CAA for his second straight year. Daly missed five games in February 2018 with a sprained ankle. He joined [[Devon Saddler]] and [[Jawan Carter]] as the only players in school history to reach 1,000 career points in their first two seasons, as he scored exactly 1,000. Following his sophomore season, Daly announced that he would transfer from Delaware.{{cite web |last1=Tresolini |first1=Kevin |title=A bolt from the Blue Hens as leading scorer Daly decides to transfer |url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/college/ud/2018/03/23/bolt-blue-hens-leading-scorer-daly-decides-transfer/454680002/ |website=[[The News Journal]] |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=March 23, 2018}} ===Saint Joseph's=== On April 9, 2018, Daly revealed that he was transferring to [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]] over offers from [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]] and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].{{cite web |last1=Tresolini |first1=Kevin |title=Family ties make Saint Joseph's logical transfer destination as ex-Hen Daly joins Hawks |url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/college/ud/2018/04/09/family-ties-make-saint-josephs-logical-transfer-destination-ex-hen-daly-joins-hawks/499194002/ |website=[[The News Journal]] |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=April 9, 2018}} He sat out his next season due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] transfer rules.{{cite web |last1=Jensen |first1=Mike |title=Ryan Daly will be St. Joseph's focal point |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/st-joes/ryan-daly-st-josephs-hawks-basketball-billy-lange-delaware-transfer-20191101.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=November 1, 2019}} On January 11, 2020, Daly recorded 28 points and eight rebounds and made a game-tying circus shot from three-point range to force overtime in an 89–83 loss to [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]].{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Ryan |title=St. Joseph's forced overtime against Davidson after insane one-handed buzzer-beater |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/saint-josephs-basketball-ryan-daly-insane-buzzer-beater-davidson-force-overtime-233955732.html |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=January 11, 2020}} His shot was ranked number one on ''[[SportsCenter]]'''s Top 10 plays of the day.{{cite web |last1=Jensen |first1=Mike |title=Ryan Daly talks about his crazy shot, an all-transfer-home team, and other City 6 observations |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/ryan-daly-st-josephs-espn-sportscenter-top-10-davidson-20200114.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=January 14, 2020}} On February 1, Daly scored a career-high 35 points along with seven rebounds, six assists and three steals in a 78–73 loss to [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]].{{cite web |title=Daly Nets Career-High 35, But Saint Louis Holds Off Men's Basketball, 78-73 |url=https://sjuhawks.com/news/2020/2/1/daly-nets-career-high-35-but-saint-louis-holds-off-mens-basketball-78-73.aspx |publisher=Saint Joseph's University |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=February 1, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 20.6 points, 6.9 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.2 steals per game. He led the A10 conference in scoring, and led the Hawks in scoring, rebounding and assists.{{Cite web|title=Ryan Daly - 2020-21 - Men's Basketball|url=https://sjuhawks.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ryan-daly/5298|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Saint Joseph's University|language=en}} Daly averaged the most points by a Saint Joseph's player since [[Jameer Nelson]] in the [[2003–04 Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball team|2003–04 season]]. He was named to the Third Team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] and First Team All-[[Philadelphia Big 5|Big 5]].{{cite web |title=Trio of Hawks Earn Big 5 Men's Basketball Honors |url=https://sjuhawks.com/news/2020/4/15/trio-of-hawks-earn-big-5-mens-basketball-honors.aspx |publisher=Saint Joseph's University |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=April 15, 2020}} After the season, Daly declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]], before withdrawing to return to Saint Joseph's for his redshirt senior year.{{cite web |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=2020 NBA Draft Early Entry Tracker |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/08/02/2020-nba-draft-early-entry-tracker/ |website=[[NBC Sports]] |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=August 2, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Jensen |first1=Mike |title=St. Joseph's basketball star Ryan Daly waits for the next act in his career |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/st-joes/ryan-daly-st-josephs-nba-draft-coronavirus-covid-19-20200721.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |accessdate=August 9, 2020 |date=July 21, 2020}} He averaged a team-high18.5 points and 6.0 rebounds per game as a senior.{{cite news |last1=Holmes |first1=C.J. |title='He's going to earn his way': St. Joe's Ryan Daly is already creating opportunities as he pushes for the NBA |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2550020/2021/05/03/hes-going-to-earn-his-way-st-joes-ryan-daly-is-already-creating-opportunities-as-he-pushes-for-the-nba/ |access-date=October 23, 2021 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=May 3, 2021}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Daly signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] for [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news |title=Bulls' Ryan Daly: Joining Bulls for Summer League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bulls-ryan-daly-joining-bulls-for-summer-league/ |access-date=October 23, 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=July 30, 2021}} He was selected with the eighth pick of the second round of the [[2021 NBA G League draft (October)|2021 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Motor City Cruise]].{{cite web |title=2021 NBA G League Draft Board |url=https://gleague.nba.com/2021-nba-g-league-draft-order/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 23, 2021 |date=October 23, 2021}} However, he did not make the opening day roster. On December 21, 2021, Daly signed with the [[Maine Celtics]], but was waived the next day after playing one game,{{cite web|title=2021-2022 Maine Celtics Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Maine-Celtics/64/Transaction-History/2022|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 23, 2021}} being subsequently claimed off waivers by the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]].{{cite web|title=2021-2022 Agua Caliente Clippers Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Agua-Caliente-Clippers/47/Transaction-History/2022|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 23, 2021}} On January 11, 2022, Daly was reacquired and then later waived by the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 11, 2022|access-date=January 11, 2022}} Ryan was then hired by the University of Albany men's basketball team as an assistant coach in 2022. https://ualbanysports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/ryan-daly/2050. skills to corporate world |url=https://www.mainlinemedianews.com/mainlinetimes/lifestyle/brian-daly-taking-coaching-skills-to-corporate-world/article_935e20c1-854e-5a49-8ee4-eecf9580c975.html
